D-0211's defeater says: "if cycles/day and the homeostasis_causal divergence rate settle back under their ceilings once the initial post-restart transient passes ... a separate shadow_activation re-normalization is likely unnecessary ... If they stay elevated, or if the spawned follow-up job's direct measurement of shadow_activation's own raw (non-argmax) value confirms it is chronically near-saturation independent of ignition moments, size shadow_activation's own knee the same way J-0594 sized integration_drive's before building anything."

EVIDENCE. Live runtime on the option-A code (commit dbec9ba, first run at the 2026-09-08 16:42 restart): 7.13 live days in 8 windows. Du was OFF about 3 days mid-window, so the nominal 09-15 due date had only 4.54 live days (F-1568).
(1) Cycles/day did not settle. 62.65 fires per live day (full live days 62, 59, 56, 66; no decaying transient). That is 41.3 per calendar day, or 43.1 per live day counting only cycles that got past the thalamic gate, so whether it exceeds D-0148's 45 depends on a basis that neither ruling states (F-1570).
(2) Forecast divergence (the J-0677 comparator's pairing, 866 pairs): median 0.011, p90 0.232; 10.9% of pairs exceed 0.2 against 1.0% before the fix, concentrated in intervals containing a defensive ignition. Whether that breaches "more than 0.2" depends on which statistic is meant, and the ruling names none (F-1571).
(3) shadow_activation's raw value is chronically near-saturated (F-1396, extended by F-1581): 171 live samples, saturated median 0.9762 against 0.9727 for the 105-day baseline; sizing k of about 123, inside F-1396's 95-134.
Also verified: the defensive share is 48.2% (floor 25%) and no fire ever hit the per-hour cap, so D-0148's conditions 1 and 2 do not fire. The defensive channel is now largely a second clock of about 46 minutes (median gap about 46 min against a constant-inflow prediction of 45.9; none of 215 defensive fires strain-led; F-1572).

THE QUESTION IS WIDER THAN shadow_activation (F-1579 is inferred first-order arithmetic; the inflow shares are verified in F-1572). completion_tension sits at 0.91-0.92 in all 1,280 post-restart [climate] samples and supplies 54.8% of the defensive-reservoir inflow (shadow 28.7%, strain 16.5%). A live climate_state.json snapshot (2026-09-19 11:50) shows four of nine dimensions at 0.90 or above: shadow_activation 0.977, belonging_pressure 0.968, autonomy_pressure 0.934, completion_tension 0.909. A shadow-only re-knee cuts about 7-8 defensive fires per day but leaves the total near 55 per live day (still above 45) and would probably just relocate the pinned label to belonging_pressure; getting under 45 needs completion_tension re-kneed as well (total about 41). The label is not cosmetic: dominant() feeds the Executive hint and the Reflection symbol every cycle (core/orchestrator.py:957-958).

OPTIONS FOR THE GO/NO-GO: (1) re-knee shadow_activation only, shadow-first and additive. (2) Re-knee the pinned cluster (shadow_activation, completion_tension, and whichever of belonging_pressure / autonomy_pressure J-1151 confirms), the only option the arithmetic says lands under 45. (3) D-0148's option C (acute impulses): its trigger clause, pressure lagging real events by more than about 10 minutes, looks met but rests on n=10 and n=6 and is not decision-grade (F-1573, inferred). (4) Accept about 63 cycles per live day and re-base the 45 ceiling to a per-live-day figure. J-1151 (open) measures the raw histories of the other pinned dimensions so the knees can be sized. D-0148 itself is NOT reopened by this; its revisit clause fires via cycles/day per live day (basis ambiguous, see above).

WHAT THE READ FOUND. After 6.35 live days (9.93 wall days) on the post-0c3955c code (F-1574) the raise delivers: 38.1 gists per live day against the 20-34 target, and 128 LLM calls per live day against the 80-135 estimate (24.4 gists and 82 calls per wall day). But semantic active_total still grows +1,013 per live day and self +860 (pre-merge +1,160 and +1,182, so 12.6% and 27.3% easing), against intake of 1,109 and 1,151 per live day, of which memory-levels retires 8.5% and 20.5% (F-1580). The upward branch is met on its wording. The downward branch is not (F-1589): no sleep step was skipped or failing and per-cluster seconds are unchanged, but night sleeps run about 67% longer (2,310 s to 3,860 s) and the memory-levels step went from 172 s to 687 s per pass.

WHAT THIS EVIDENCE ADDS THAT D-0185's SIZING DID NOT HAVE.
(1) Kind asymmetry: per attempted cluster semantic commits 37.9% against self 79.3% (F-1585), so extra semantic cluster budget buys about 2.1x the LLM calls per committed gist; 52.4% of graded semantic clusters fail the 0.75 faithfulness floor (mechanism inferred, F-1586).
(2) The last_ts frontier makes about 98% of warm semantic rows (13,481 of 13,701, 98.4%) and about 96% of warm self rows (12,337 of 12,825, 96.2%) unreachable by memory-levels at ANY cap (F-1583; the counts were re-measured independently on 2026-09-19; code at core/memory_levels.py lines 512-519 and 602). The pipeline can only offset NEW intake, so raising caps alone can slow growth but can never shrink active_total back to the K x keep_kind budgets.
(3) The newest-160 fetch window is estimated to truncate 35-40% of runs (F-1584, INFERRED from an estimated fetch time).
(4) Parity arithmetic at observed yields is about 990 LLM calls per live day (7.7x today), above J-0690's 640-730 estimate, which assumed a blended 52% success rate (F-1580), before any fetch-window change.
(5) Each extra cluster adds about 83 s to a serial sleep pipeline whose memory-levels step is already 687 s per pass (F-1589).

WHAT WAS RUN. The live _SCAN_SYS at production settings (temperature 0.3, 400 tokens, json) on 96 real reconstructed (thought, active-list) inputs since 2026-09-02T21:07:50Z (seeded strata; the templated book-finish rows EXCLUDED), 40 of them repeated to 3 identical runs, plus 12 synthetic clear-case controls and the three templated strings as an identical-input probe; every verdict scored through the real formation gate. Baseline = today's seat, qwen3.5:9b (:11433). Candidates = granite3.1-moe:3b (:11437) and gemma4:12b (:11439). command-r7b (:11441), the candidate D-0176 named first, COULD NOT BE TESTED: its hub timed out on 8 of 8 attempts in the window, and telemetry shows 46.5 percent of its calls failing over the last 7 days (100 percent on 09-22). falcon3:7b (:11440) and mixtral:8x7b (:11438) were another lab's exclusive hubs this window and are untested.

NUMBERS (n and 95 percent intervals are in the findings):
                                                      qwen3.5:9b (baseline) | granite3.1-moe:3b | gemma4:12b

 load_bearing flag missing from a reported stand               0 percent | 46 percent (says false in 1 of 227 stands) | 0 percent
 non-stand thoughts formed (blind independent read, n=68)      52 percent | 50 percent | 40 percent (p=0.23 vs baseline: not significant)
 chore-like thoughts formed (blind, n=28)                      46 percent | 57 percent | 46 percent
 F-0677 narrow bucket rejected (regex, n=24; no labels)        21 percent | 42 percent (flag missing) | 62 percent (p=0.008)

READING. (1) The current seat is noisy on its own: on 40 percent (16 of 40) of identical real inputs it flips formed/not formed between three identical runs, and the templated ask-the-library string is formed 2 and rejected 3 times in 5 identical prompts, which is F-0770's failure mode reproduced on qwen3.5:9b. At temperature 0 all of that vanishes (0/20 flips, byte-identical outputs; F-1693), so it is sampling noise, curable at the call with no model change; a residual context sensitivity remains (the same thought under a different real active list flips the gate in 6/32 swaps at temperature 0). (2) The ledger itself is lenient. I read all 96 thoughts against the prompt's own categories (inferred, one reader): none holds a clear stand (0 clear, 7 ambiguous, 37 chore-like, 38 description or musing, 14 idle wants), yet the ledger formed 53 percent of the blind non-stand thoughts (36/68). So agreement with the ledger's history is a weak yardstick and the baseline's own re-run agreement (67 percent) is only a test-retest ceiling; the hold-rate north-star is computed over formed stands that, on this read, come almost entirely from thoughts holding no clear stand (of the 60 historically formed cases in the sample: 55 chore-like, descriptive or idle-want thoughts, 5 ambiguous, none a clear stand). (3) granite3.1-moe:3b is unfit: it fails the controls, leaves the load_bearing flag out in 46 percent of its stands, almost never says false, never returns null, copies the whole thought as the stand in half its reports, and is as inconsistent as the baseline (18/40 gate flips, 33/40 full-verdict flips); this matches sitting's own granite audition. (4) gemma4:12b is FIT for the task but is not shown to be MORE ACCURATE than the incumbent: it follows the contract (controls 24/24, no missing flags), is far more stable on identical input at the production temperature, rejects every one of the three templated strings in every run (0 formed of 27, including 0 of 12 under four different real active lists, against the baseline's 5 formed of 27; p=0.05), and rejects the F-0677 narrow-bucket regex set more often (62 vs 21 percent, p=0.008); but on my blind read it forms somewhat fewer non-stands than the baseline (40 vs 52 percent, not significant) and exactly as many chore-like thoughts (46 percent each). Its costs: it forms fewer stands (33 percent of the 96 sampled cases against 56 percent for the baseline's re-run; 48 against 60 percent weighted to the natural stream, so roughly a fifth to two-fifths fewer; 43 percent recall against the ledger; null on 55 percent of runs), it is a CPU model (median 21 s, p90 48 s: fine for a fire-and-forget scan on a 60 s cooldown, but the supervisor launches its hub lazy with idle-unload 300 s, so at about 263 scans a day, with gaps of several minutes, it would often meet a cold load), and its family (Google) differs from the qwen generator. (5) command-r7b: no classification evidence, and on availability alone it is the weakest named seat.

RECOMMENDATION (yours to rule; nothing depends on my having chosen). (a) Do not seat granite3.1-moe:3b. (b) Regardless of the seat, set scan_shadow's temperature to 0.0 (or at most 0.1): it removes the identical-input flip on the current seat (measured, F-1693) and should on any greedy-decoded seat. That is the cheapest fix for F-0770's failure mode and needs no decision about models. (c) The seat itself is mainly a decoupling question, not an accuracy one: the only accuracy-type advantage measured for gemma4:12b is on the mechanical F-0677 regex bucket (62 vs 21 percent rejected); the controls tie and the blind read is a wash on chores and not significant on non-stands, so the case for moving is the decoupled-judge law itself (F-0948: the generator should not judge its own output) plus stable output and a somewhat stricter gate. If you want that, gemma4:12b is the only tested candidate fit to take the seat and is my recommended pick, on the understanding that you are accepting a stricter gate (a fifth to two-fifths fewer formed stands, so the hold-rate is re-baselined once after at least one day or 250 cycles, as J-0533 did) rather than a like-for-like swap. A cautious path in this project's style: run gemma4:12b as a SHADOW scanner beside the incumbent for a week, logging both verdicts, before switching.
